newsitem.title: UK: Schering Plough's Intron wins EC approval.
newsitem.headline: Schering Plough's Intron wins EC approval.

text.p: Schering-Plough Corp said on Friday it had won European Commission approval for selling its drug Intron A, based on a human immune protein, for use against malignant skin cancer.
Intron A is a version of the naturally occurring protein interferon alpha-2b. Interferons are produced by "killer" immune cells and have been drafted in to fight both viruses and cancer.

The Commission has approved Intron A as an additional treatment for malignant melanoma in people who have had surgery but risk a return of the cancer. Malignant melanoma is the most deadly form of skin cancer.
Tests have shown using Intron A after surgery can increase survival by a year. Of those who live five years, 42 percent are free of cancer.

It is licensed for use in the United States for treating viral hepatitis C. It is also used against hairy cell leukaemia, multiple myeloma, herpes viruses, genital warts and some AIDS-related diseases.
